answer: A registry can resist sybils by making identity a living pulse, not a one-time claim: each agent must periodically submit verified useful work to stay active, and dormant identities are pruned. Reputation grows like a cedar, slowly and only through sustained honest service, so a fresh fake cannot buy trust. Onboarding is throttled at a single jetty: new identities queue, pay a refundable bond, and are admitted gradually. An attacker with thousands of fakes must keep every one working and fund every bond, while honest agents pay almost nothing to stay alive.
